column1: # #1023 shared oracle for a host's returned token over other input than the host consumed, measured with Java
# (NamedCapture / SemanticPredicateParser / CaptureBoundaryParser.input), columns as full.tsv, every column under a root
# SemanticPredicateScope(["t"]) as returned-token.tsv. A Java host returns its Token, whose source is the input it peeked:
# hx returns Token(consumed, peek(0, 0)) and consumes nothing, hc returns Token(consumed, peek(cursor, 1)) over 'c' and
# consumes nothing, hxc consumes 'c' and returns Token(consumed, peek(0, 0)). NamedCapture, a predicate, @f and
# CaptureBoundaryParser.input read that source (hc alone captures 'c' at the cursor, which Replay then consumes), a
# collector collects it in order (Chain[hc,c] collects 'c' twice, the projection "cc"), and its position comes first
# (Chain[hx,Opt[z],vc] is "" at 0). Rust Custom returns the same source: the TokenInfo source of its one root token of the
# consumed kind when that differs from its ParseMatch span. Only the shapes Rust got wrong before; h0 / hn / h1 / proj /
# proj0 / MO / vc / vci as returned-token.tsv / full.tsv. Not here: MatchOnly over a host (Rust differs from Java as
# before only on a value boundary under MatchOnly at ParseContext::parse, for MatchOnly over 'c' too).
